Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: burst behavior and SLAs (post-demo)

Jonas, Ben — thanks for yesterday's demo. A few concrete follow-ups from our SRE team: we run intermittent card verification workloads where token-sized streaming responses matter (partial auth tokens returned as they arrive). Our current baseline: 150 RPS sustained for 10s bursts, p95 latency target <= 180ms for 512-token responses (tokenization + streaming start). During a 10x unexpected spike we need graceful degradation (queueing or fallback to lower-capacity model) with max queuing < 2s and a clear failover to a cached local policy after 5s.

Can Redwood confirm:
- expected scale-up time to add capacity when moving from 0 to 200 concurrent LLM streams,
- warm pool sizing you recommend for <200ms p95 preservation, and
- how streaming partial output handoff is handled when prewarmed instances become available mid-stream?

Attached is a small extract of our production pattern and a CSV of recent spikes. Happy to set a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Dunn
Head of Platform Reliability, EdgePay
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Claire Dunn <claire@edgepay.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: burst behavior and SLAs (post-demo)

Claire — great notes, thanks for the data. Short answers up-front, then a suggested plan and owners.

Summary answers:
- Scale-up to add capacity (cold start): typical additional instance availability ~18-28s depending on GPU class and model footprint; warm-pool activation is ~300-700ms to accept traffic once prewarmed, so warm pools are the main lever for sub-second activation.
- Warm pool sizing: for your 150 RPS 10s bursts and 512-token responses, our back-of-envelope recommends a warm pool of ~6 medium GPUs for free scaling headroom (we'll model exact numbers in the spreadsheet).
- Streaming handoff mid-stream: Redwood supports connection-level streaming with a seamless handoff only when using the same model variant; if a new instance becomes available mid-response we continue streaming from the original KV-cache-backed process unless the request is retried — for long-lived streams we recommend sticky routing + prewarmed capacity to avoid mid-stream transfer.

Proposed plan (short):
1) Redwood modeling session — run the attached surge-modeling.xlsx with your CSV to produce a checkpoint matrix (owner: Ben; due: Wed 2026-05-20).
2) Warm-pool sizing and spike sim — agree concrete warm pool counts for the three tiers (owner: Monica; due: Thu 2026-05-21).
3) Streaming acceptance test — schedule a 30-minute replay test that validates p95 and max queue <2s and verifies partial token behavior under failover (owner: Laura; due: Fri 2026-05-22).
4) Draft SLO checkpoint doc with gating thresholds and fallback policies (owner: Jonas; due: Mon 2026-05-25).

I'll attach a quick checklist and the preliminary SLO matrix. If this looks good, can we lock a 30-minute slot Thu 5/21 10:00-10:30 PT for the modeling walkthrough?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: burst behavior and SLAs (post-demo)

Looping in a few details on modeling assumptions so our numbers match EdgePay's expectations. I started filling edgepay-surge-modeling.xlsx with assumptions based on Claire's CSV. Key points I'm encoding:
- Model footprint: 11.3GB KV + 2.2GB params working set for the 512-token path (we need Claire to confirm model variant).
- Concurrency per GPU: with our continuous-batching heuristics a medium GPU (A10-class) sustains ~24 concurrent short-streams at 512 tokens with p95 ~160-200ms.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive scale-up on p95 drift > 15% for 30s window, scale-down after 3m of underutilization. This keeps transient spikes from thrashing but still responds in seconds when warm pools are available.
- Queueing behavior: we implement a weighted queue that prioritizes reconnecting streaming sessions; we can expose a client-side header for soft-priority to avoid dropping auth flows. Configurable max queue timeout = 2s (recommended).

Ask: Claire — can you confirm the model variant and whether you prefer a hard failover (instant cached policy) or a soft degraded mode (reduced token rate) after 5s? That choice affects warm-pool sizing and whether we keep an extra 1-2 GPUs as buffer.

I'll have the first modeling pass by end of day Wed.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks actionable. Quick answers:
- Model variant: production-auth-v2 (quantized, 8-bit).
- Failover preference: hard failover to cached policy after 5s for payment authorization paths (we cannot risk partial authorizations). For logging/tracing flows we can do soft degradation.

Thu 5/21 10:00 PT works for the 30-minute modeling walkthrough — please send calendar invite. We'll bring a member of our streaming infra team to validate the handoff flow.

Claire
Claire Dunn
Head of Platform Reliability, EdgePay
